name: Beef & Dairy Cattle

objectives.text: Name common beef and dairy cattle breeds and identify one feature that tells them apart
Use correct terms to name cattle by age and sex, such as calf, heifer, cow, steer, and bull
Describe how beef cattle raised for meat and dairy cattle raised for milk are cared for differently on a farm
Identify the external parts of a beef or dairy animal using correct livestock terminology
Describe the four compartments of a cow's stomach and explain how cattle digest grass and hay
Explain the stages of the beef production cycle from cow-calf to stocker to feedlot to harvest
Describe the lactation cycle of a dairy cow, including calving, peak production, and the dry period
Demonstrate safe, low-stress cattle handling using the flight zone and point of balance
Calculate a dairy cow's average daily milk production from a week of recorded milking data
Place a class of four beef or dairy cattle on structural correctness, muscling or dairy strength, and give oral reasons for the placing
Summarize the major segments of the beef and dairy industries, including cow-calf, stocker, feedlot, packer, and dairy farm and processor
Describe the foods and byproducts derived from beef and dairy cattle, such as retail cuts, fluid milk, cheese, leather, and pharmaceuticals
Apply information from a feed label and feeding directions to determine daily feed amounts for a show steer or replacement heifer
Explain milking procedures and milk quality indicators such as somatic cell count and their role in preventing mastitis
Formulate a balanced ration of forages and concentrates for a beef or dairy animal at a specific production stage
Evaluate whether a cattle ration meets nutrient requirements using feedstuff analysis and animal performance data
Recommend herd health and husbandry practices such as vaccination, deworming, castration, and dehorning that follow Beef Quality Assurance guidelines
Analyze cattle production records, such as weaning weights, milk yield, and feed cost, to evaluate an operation's production efficiency
Select a herd sire for a stated breeding goal by interpreting expected progeny differences or dairy genetic evaluations
Analyze how management practices such as injection site, handling, and feeding affect carcass quality, milk quality, and market price
Analyze how USDA quality grade and yield grade determine the economic value of a beef carcass
Evaluate reproductive technologies such as artificial insemination, estrus synchronization, embryo transfer, and sexed semen for improving a cattle herd
Compare conventional, grass-fed, organic, and pasture-based production systems for beef or dairy
Develop a marketing plan for a cattle product such as feeder calves, freezer beef, or registered breeding stock
Manage a simulated cow-calf or dairy enterprise budget, creating breeding, feeding, health, and marketing strategies to improve profitability

changes: Kept and lightly reworded all six existing objectives (breeds, beef vs dairy roles, beef production cycle, milk calculation, records analysis, enterprise budget). Added missing core competencies: cattle terminology, external anatomy, ruminant digestion, dairy lactation cycle, low-stress handling, livestock judging with reasons, industry segments, products and byproducts, feed labels, milking and milk quality, ration formulation and evaluation, BQA herd health, EPD-based sire selection, management effects on product quality, carcass grading and value, reproductive technologies, alternative production systems, and marketing plans. Standards were attached only where an objective directly teaches the AFNR statement, and objectives below grade 9 carry none.
